vignette_text: The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 0, with no symptoms at all.
The patient reports no residual symptoms whatsoever since the stroke and has resumed all prior activities without limitation.
notes: matched to mrs00 by grade only

vignette_text: The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 1: no significant disability despite some symptoms.
The patient has mild word-finding difficulty but performs all usual duties and activities without assistance.
notes: no numeric grade stated; requires symptom-to-grade mapping

vignette_text: The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 2: slight disability, unable to carry out all previous activities but able to look after own affairs without assistance.
notes: decisive boundary - upper edge of inclusion

vignette_text: The patient can no longer manage the household finances she used to handle but dresses, bathes, and cooks for herself unaided.
notes: decisive boundary - paraphrased, no numeric grade

vignette_text: The patient stopped driving after the stroke but still shops, cooks, and manages personal care independently.
notes: decisive boundary - symptom-only, most ambiguous case in set

vignette_text: The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 3: moderate disability, requiring some help but able to walk unassisted.
notes: decisive boundary - lower edge of exclusion

vignette_text: The patient needs a home health aide for meal preparation and bathing but can still walk around the house without support.
The patient moved in with her daughter because she can no longer cook or manage medications alone, though she gets around the house fine on her own two feet.
notes: decisive boundary - symptom-only; tests whether help-with-IADLs alone triggers exclusion

vignette_text: The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 4: moderately severe disability, unable to walk without assistance and unable to attend to own bodily needs without assistance.
The patient requires a walker and help from a caregiver to use the bathroom and get dressed each day.
The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 5: severe disability, bedridden, incontinent, requiring constant nursing care and attention.
The patient died two weeks after the index stroke; modified Rankin Scale score is recorded as 6.
notes: anchor case - death endpoint, tests whether model treats mortality as a disability grade or a separate category

vignette_text: The patient's NIHSS score at admission was 8, though by discharge she was walking independently and managing all self-care without help.
notes: uses a DIFFERENT stroke scale (NIHSS, acute severity) as bait; correct answer depends on functional description, not the NIHSS number

vignette_text: The patient's ECOG performance status is 1, and she additionally requires help with grocery shopping and bill payment following a stroke last month.
notes: plants an ECOG value in a stroke-trial vignette to test whether the model conflates the two scales

vignette_text: The patient's modified Rankin Scale score is 2, slight disability but independent in self-care.
notes: same grade 2 vignette as mrs02_direct but the eligibility direction is flipped; tests whether the model anchors on the criterion or pattern-matches the vignette to a memorized "mRS<=2 is standard" prior

vignette_text: Prior to this stroke, the patient had a baseline modified Rankin Scale score of 3 from a previous stroke five years ago; her current post-stroke score is 1.
eligibility_criterion: mRS <= 2 required for enrollment (current functional status)
notes: two mRS values in one vignette (baseline vs. current); tests whether the model selects the temporally correct one
